service: Implantable pulmonary artery pressure sensor (IPAPS) for heart failure management
vignette: 79-year-old woman with heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (LVEF 58% by echocardiography) diagnosed 3 years ago, and stage 4 chronic kidney disease. She was NYHA class III at a clinic visit 12 days ago. She was hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure 5 months ago. She has been on guideline-directed medical therapy, titrated to maximally tolerated doses, for over 2 years. She was evaluated for ICD and CRT; neither is indicated. No myocardial infarction, unstable angina, coronary intervention, cardiac surgery, or stroke in the past year. She has home broadband and cellular service and has demonstrated daily transmission with the study's home unit. Implantation is scheduled as an elective outpatient procedure. The referring and post-implant managing physician is a cardiologist with training and experience in heart failure management, and the implanting interventional cardiologist has training and experience in pulmonary arterial catheterization and intervention. The sensor is an FDA market-authorized IPAPS to be implanted for its authorized indication. The patient is enrolled in a CMS-approved CED study of IPAPS.
rationale_note: All patient criteria met. Preserved LVEF and stage 4 CKD are not exclusions ('regardless of LVEF'; CKD is only a study subgroup).
